findings.title: TotalDocs iterates the index cache without holding cacheMu, racing with BuildIndex writes
findings.body: `TotalDocs()` ranges over `b.cache` without taking `b.cacheMu` (read) lock, while `BuildIndex` now writes into `b.cache` under a short-lived write lock (lines 137-139). This is a genuine data race that Go turns into a fatal runtime error ("concurrent map iteration and map write"), which crashes the process. The new call site makes it reachable: `searchSupport.init` starts the watch-event goroutine (search.go lines 207-213) and only afterwards logs `s.search.TotalDocs()` (search.go line 216); any watch event handled in that goroutine can call `getOrCreateIndex` -> `build` -> `BuildIndex`, writing the map while `TotalDocs` is iterating. `TotalDocs` should take `cacheMu.RLock()`.

findings.title: Removing the BuildIndex-wide lock allows two concurrent builds of the same key
findings.body: `BuildIndex` no longer holds `cacheMu` for the duration of the build; it only locks when inserting into the cache. Because `searchSupport.getOrCreateIndex` checks `GetIndex` and then calls `BuildIndex` without any per-key serialization, two callers (e.g. a search request and a watch event for the same namespace/group/resource) can now build the same index concurrently. For file-backed indexes both goroutines call `bleve.New` on the same directory `b.opts.Root/<ns>/<resource>.<group>` at the same time, which can fail or corrupt the on-disk index; both also increment `IndexMetrics.IndexTenants` and the second cache write silently discards the first index (leaking its open bleve index/file handles). Some form of per-key locking (e.g. a keyed mutex / single-flight) is needed to keep the previous mutual exclusion while still allowing different keys to build in parallel.

findings.title: Cancel function leaked when Init fails in NewResourceServer
findings.body: `ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(...)` is created at line 229, but on the new error path `s.Init(ctx)` -> `return nil, err` (lines 258-262) `cancel()` is never called. The context is never cancelled, so any background work tied to it (and the context itself) is leaked, and the partially-initialized server's goroutines (e.g. the SQL poller / watch goroutines started during `search.init`) keep running for the lifetime of the process even though the constructor reported failure. `go vet`'s lostcancel check will also flag this. Call `cancel()` before returning the error.

findings.title: Full index build now happens synchronously inside the constructor with no deadline or cancellation
findings.body: `NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` with the server's own background context, which runs `lifecycle.Init`, the complete search index build over every namespace, and `initWatcher`. The constructor is invoked from the service-wiring path, so Grafana/storage-server startup is blocked for as long as indexing takes (minutes for large installations) and there is no way for the caller to pass a deadline or cancel the work - the caller's context is ignored and the internal context is only cancelled by `Stop`, which can't run yet. Consider accepting a context (or running the index build in the background and gating only search on it) so startup cannot hang indefinitely.

findings.title: After Stop(), requests are no longer rejected because no method checks initErr anymore
findings.body: `Stop` communicates shutdown exclusively by setting `s.initErr` to "service is stopping"/"service is stopped", which used to be surfaced because every RPC method began with `if err := s.Init(ctx); err != nil`. Those checks were all removed in this PR, so `s.initErr` is now write-only dead state: after `Stop` cancels the background context, Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/blob calls still execute and will fail with opaque "context canceled" errors or operate against a torn-down backend instead of returning the clear "service is stopping" error. A explicit stopped/closed flag checked by the public methods (or returning an error from the entry points) is needed to preserve the previous contract.

findings.title: Shared err and totalBatchesIndexed are mutated from errgroup goroutines (data race)
findings.body: Inside `init`, each `group.Go` closure assigns to the enclosing `err` variable (`_, _, err = s.build(...)`) and increments the enclosing `totalBatchesIndexed`. With `initWorkers > 1` these run concurrently, so both are unsynchronized writes to shared variables: `go test -race` will flag it, the reported batch count can be wrong, and the `err` returned by one goroutine can be overwritten by another before `group.Wait()` observes it, so a build failure may be silently hidden or a spurious error attributed. Use local variables inside the closure (`idxErr := ...; return idxErr`) and an atomic counter.

findings.title: BuildIndex span context is still discarded, so child spans do not nest under it
findings.body: This PR's stated goal is fixing trace propagation (the callers in search.go and sql/backend.go were changed from `_, span :=` to `ctx, span :=`), but `bleveBackend.BuildIndex` still does `_, span := b.tracer.Start(ctx, ...)` and the builder callback keeps using the caller's context. As a result the storage `ListIterator` spans emitted while building are siblings of the `unified_search.bleve.BuildIndex` span rather than children, leaving BuildIndex as a leaf in traces and defeating the purpose of the change.

findings.title: Postgres integration coverage for the storage-server target is silently disabled
findings.body: The only integration test that boots the `StorageServer` target (and therefore exercises the new eager `NewResourceServer` initialization path) is now skipped for postgres with only a TODO comment. Combined with the existing sqlite skip, this leaves mysql as the sole DB covered, so a startup regression specific to postgres - plausible given init now runs synchronously at construction - would go undetected. The skip should reference a tracking issue or the failure should be diagnosed before merge.
